I once read a book on how to become an employed writer - written by employed writers. There are hundreds of different ways to do it if one is so inclined. The major point of the book was writers have to write - a lot - so it really needs to be something you enjoy doing.

I have written a lot over the years - but I am generally too long winded for most people - and I know that. I could probably carve out a niche somewhere if I really wanted to. I say you should do your own thing - you'll be happiest that way. If it should turn out to be financially lucrative, all the better. Like most everything, the more you write, the better you become at it.

Blogging has really opened the doors for writers, because now you can publish your stuff for free, build your own audience, earn your own traffic, and through that generate revenue - even sell stuff on the side and obtain sponsors. All without a publisher - and just how many books are being read these days? How many newspapers are still sold? You get the point. You don't need anybody anymore, and are free to just go wherever the winds will take you.

I got into computers - started as a hobby in the 1980's - built that into a small empire in the 1990's - because I enjoyed it. It wasn't like work to me, even as I was putting in 16 hour days. I still build amazing computers years after I closed that business, and I am still gaming. Follow your passion - hook up with like minded individuals - do your own thing as best you can, and the money will usually follow.
